newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury shares fall over eight percent.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury shares fall over eight percent.

text.p: Shares in UK supermarket group J Sainsbury opened sharply lower on Friday following a warning from the company that current year profits would fall short of analysts expectations.
The shares were down 33-1/2p at 358-1/2p by 0810 GMT, dragging the rest of the sector down as well.
Shares in Tesco fell 6-1/2p or 1.77 percent to 361-1/2p, Asda was down 2-1/4p or 1.8 percent to 122p and Safeway was 14p or 3.3 percent lower at 388p.

But one leading industry analyst said that the disappointment was specific to Sainsbury. The analyst said his advice to investors was "not to panic with the others in the sector...it's just a knee-jerk reaction."
Earlier, Sainsbury announced a 4.4 percent rise in like-for-like sales over the eight week Christmas trading period but added that the cost of building sales had hurt profits.
"Obviously others in the sector are exerting considerable pressure on Sainsbury," said the analyst. "And it's Tesco and Safeway that are winning the day."
Sainsbury warned that annual profits would be around 640-650 million stg before a 50 million stg charge, about 150 million stg below analysts estimates.

"The like-for-like sales growth was broadly in line with forecasts but clearly the profits warning was a shock," the analyst said. "The sales growth they have seen has been pretty much bought, and it seems to be costing Sainsbury's more than the others." "It's setting an uncomfortable precedent."
